answer.origin: Primary source: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR, filed August 17, 2026), Items 1.01, 2.03 and 7.01, with a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. Event and statement date are both August 17, 2026. No independent or secondary confirmation was supplied.
answer.note: Stated fact: on August 17, 2026 NVIDIA entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as Lessor, covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load in aggregate at the Portsmouth Site (PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio). OpenAI Group PBC affiliate is the tenant. NVIDIA may provide credit support for about an additional 3.8 GW at its sole discretion. NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation is capped cumulatively at $105 billion for the initial commitment. Payments are subject to conditions including Lessor satisfaction of ready-for-service conditions, expected beginning in 2028. On a Trigger Event (OpenAI insolvency causing lease default, or OpenAI payment failure), NVIDIA pays generally the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and amounts recovered via replacement lease or sale. NVIDIA may then assume, relet, sell, allow termination, or defer remedies up to one year. Obligations end at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, lease termination by OpenAI, OpenAI reaching a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events. OpenAI agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts actually paid. The filing also states OpenAI will use capacity supporting about 4.25 GW of IT load to deploy NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, subject to limited exceptions. What it supports about the business: NVIDIA has an undertaken, capped, contingent guarantee exposure of up to $105 billion tied to a specific multi-gigawatt campus, and the filing says the campus is intended to host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure. Conditional interpretation: if the guaranty is called, it would be a large contingent cash obligation for NVIDIA, partly offset by OpenAI reimbursement. Its size relative to NVIDIA's own financials is not established by the source. The demand link to NVIDIA product sales is a hypothesis: the filing says the tenant will deploy the DSX platform, but it gives no NVIDIA revenue, order, pricing or purchase amount for this site. The guaranty could be true while NVIDIA product sales to the site are small or are made through other channels, so the product-demand link needs the missing premise of a disclosed supply or purchase relationship.
limitations: The full text of the Agreements is not available; the source says the form will be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, so guaranteed minimum values, lease terms and termination mechanics are known only as summarized.
The filing does not define IT load relative to total facility power, so the conversion from 4.25 GW or 3.8 GW to dollars or to NVIDIA product content is not established.

The $105 billion cap is stated for the initial commitment; the source does not say how it is allocated across the 4.25 GW, whether it covers the 3.8 GW expansion, or what the expected loss on a Trigger Event would be.
No payments made or expected to be made under the Agreements are disclosed; the timing of any payment beyond the expected 2028 ready-for-service start is not stated.
The source does not disclose the accounting treatment of the guaranty, its fair value, or whether it is recorded as a liability or disclosed only as a commitment.
OpenAI's credit standing, its reimbursement capacity, and the terms and sufficiency of the indemnity are not assessed in the source.
No NVIDIA revenue, order, supply or pricing amount tied to the Portsmouth Site or to the DSX platform for this site is disclosed; the source states deployment intent only.
The SB Energy construction, financing and power arrangements are not described beyond the ready-for-service condition, so project delivery risk is unassessed.
No historical records, prior NVIDIA disclosures about SB Energy or the Portsmouth Site, or comparable guaranty arrangements were supplied, so consistency with prior statements cannot be checked.
follow_up: Obtain the filed Agreements exhibit from the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026 and check guaranteed minimum values, lease terms, cap allocation, and whether the 3.8 GW expansion is covered by the $105 billion cap.
Check NVIDIA's 10-Q and subsequent 10-K for disclosure of the guaranty as a commitment or contingent liability, its fair value, and any accrual.
Check the Exhibit 99.1 press release and SB Energy or OpenAI public statements for the financing, power, construction schedule and tenant commitments for the Portsmouth Site.
Check whether NVIDIA's disclosed product revenue or customer concentration in later filings references the Portsmouth Site, OpenAI, or DSX platform deployments, to test the product-demand hypothesis.
Check OpenAI public statements or credit disclosures for its capacity to meet lease payments and reimburse NVIDIA under the indemnity.
